about: Who pays each revenue line no flow in the town pays, and when. A line here is paid by a named group of payers (a counted group at the coarser level: businesses, importers, estates, vehicle owners elsewhere) in installments on its due month and day, as a transfer to the treasury that records the payer and the due date (`treasury-tax`, or the row's own `transfer` kind for a line that is not a tax). A line not here is still the monthly stand-in (stopgap SG-GOV-outside-revenue-monthly).

corporateIncomeTax.source: Internal Revenue Code section 6655(c) and (i): a calendar-year corporation pays estimated tax in four installments due on the 15th of April, June, September and December. State and local corporate taxes follow the federal dates.

customsDuties.source: 19 CFR 24.25: duties on a periodic monthly statement are due on the 15th working day of the following month, about the 21st of the calendar month.

payer.name: Makers and sellers of taxed goods

exciseTaxes.source: 26 CFR 40.6302(c)-1 and 48.6302(c)-1: federal excise taxes are deposited semimonthly, by the 14th and the 29th of the month; the monthly close takes one installment per month at mid-month.
exciseTaxes.spread: Any day from the 14th to the 29th.

estateAndGiftTaxes.source: Internal Revenue Code sections 6075 and 6151: estate tax is due nine months after death and gift tax with the April return. Deaths are spread through the year, so installments are monthly.
estateAndGiftTaxes.spread: Gift tax lands in April; estate tax is spread.

payer.name: Sellers of fuel, tobacco, alcohol and other taxed goods

selectiveSalesTaxes.source: Most states take monthly returns for motor fuel, tobacco and alcohol taxes due on the 20th of the following month (Federation of Tax Administrators, state tax calendars).

payer.name: Vehicle owners, licensees and other taxpayers

vehicleAndOtherTaxes.source: Registrations and licenses renew through the year, so the revenue arrives in monthly installments (state motor vehicle agencies).

payer.name: People elsewhere who use the government's services

chargesAndFees.source: Charges for services are paid as the services are used through the year (fares and utility bills monthly, tuition by term, hospital bills as care is given), so the part paid by people outside the town arrives in monthly installments. The town's own households pay their part out of their living costs (budgets-service-charges.ts), and that comes off each installment.
chargesAndFees.spread: Tuition lands at the start of each term; fares and utility bills are monthly.
